# . . . Preface . . .

THIS number of the Kentucky Statute Service contains all the laws enacted by the 1922, 1924 and 1926 sessions of the General Assembly and is the only codification of the statute laws of a general and permanent nature recording the action of the General Assembly and of the Court of Appeals since the 1922 compilation of the Kentucky Statutes. All additions to the laws there compiled and all amendments, revisions, repeals, etc., of the sections of the permanent volume are here set forth in the language of the official Session Acts of 1922, 1924 and 1926 as these acts have been construed by the Court of Appeals.

The existing status of any section of the Kentucky Statutes can be determined immediately by reference, first, to the permanent, bound volume and then to this supplement. It is cumulative and contains *all the matter of the previous bi-ennial supplements* as changed by the law making and construing branches of the state government. It "keeps the Statutes to date" as the publishers promised.

The entire contents have been printed from type entirely re-set throughout. Mr. Henry Pirtle, formerly of the Louisville bar, has again been retained to edit the text of the laws. His past experience in this connection as editor of the third volume (1918) of the preceding edition of the Kentucky Statutes, of the 1919 edition of the Kentucky Codes of Civil and Criminal Practice and of other Kentucky practice books during the past ten years, and his painstaking efforts to produce an accurate and complete codification of the Kentucky statute law will, we believe, be reflected in the following pages.

The profession will be pleased to know that the publishers are so fortunate as to have retained the services of Judge Richard Priest Dietzman, of the Kentucky Court of Appeals, to annotate the decisions of the court which construe and apply the Kentucky Constitution and Statutes, for inclusion in this number. The bar has long acknowledged the aid received from the annotations prepared by the late Judge Charles B. Seymour whose work Judge Dietzman continues. The annotations supplement those in the permanent volume and cover all sections of the Kentucky Statutes which have been referred to or applied by the court in opinions rendered through volume 214 of the Kentucky Reports. Parallel citations to the Southwestern Reporter are included. Through the use of the "Key Number" in the Southwestern ready reference is had to the decisions of other jurisdictions construing similar statutes.

The publishers earnestly solicit suggestions for the improvement of the Service to make the codification more perfect from year to year.

THE BALDWIN LAW PUBLISHING COMPANY

September 15, 1926.

Officers who saw a man operating a moonshine

Goodloe , 195 Ky . 240 , 242 § . W. 632 .
This section does not render inadmissible evidence

Evidence obtained by a search by federal officers

§ 49. Indebtedness that may be created.
The general assembly cannot incur indebtedness
in excess of $500,000. An excess of obligations
(other than governmental expenses ) above the reve-
nues for a fiscalyear is indebtedness . Construction
or maintenance of highways is not a governmental
expense . A valid deficitin any department is in-
debtedness . Billeterv . State Highway Commission ,
203 Ky . 15 , 261 S. W. 855 .
The generalassemblycannotauthorizethe state
highway commission to let contracts aggregating
in ultimate cost more than revenues of two years .
Federal aid and certain donations and tax on gaso-
line and certain licenses are available revenue .
Billeterv. State Highway Commission, 203 Ky . 15,
261 S. W. 855 .
§ 50. Indebtedness; submission of ques-
tion .
Obligations incurred by the Commonwealth to a
county under Act of March 16, 1920 , (c. 17 р . 76,

An action under this section may be barred by
limitation. This section does not relate to negligent
acts in operating a railroad. Chesapeake & Ohio
Railroad Co. v . Scott,197 Ky . 636, 247 S. W. 735 .
This section applies to the construction of a pub-
lic road across land privately owned . McDonald v .
Powell county ,199 Ky .300 ,250 S. W. 1007 .
A city may authorize a railroad company to con-
struct along itsstreetstracks which encroach on the
part reserved for sidewalks. P. Bannen Pipe Co.
v . IllinoisCentral R. R. Co., 203 Ky . 659, 262 S. W.
111 .
Where privatepropertyisdamaged on account of
diversionof a stream resultingfrom county permit-
tingdriftto accumulate againsta trestlesupporting
a highway bridge, the county is liablein damages .
Letcher County v . Hogg , 209 Ky . 182 , 272 S.W. 423 .
A county which constructs a turnpike so as to
throw water on adjoining property must respond in
damages for such taking . Black Mountain Corpo-
rationv.Houston,211 Ky .621, 277 S.W. 993.

This section is mandatory and self-executing . It
limits the sheriff'sright to retain commissions on
taxes collected. A taxpayer having vainly de-
manded that the county attorney sue, had a right
of action to recover for the county an excess of
fees received by a sheriff. The Commonwealth was
not a necessary party to the action. Shipp v .
Rogers ; Shipp v .Bradley ; 196 Ky .523 ,247 S. W. 157 .
The sheriffmay be requiredby the county to ac-
count for all moneys received by him as compen-
sation in excess of the salary provided and compen-
sationfor his deputiesand assistants. Common-
wealth v. Nunnelley, 211 Ky . 409, 277 S.W. 506.
§ 247. Printingand binding to be letto
lowest bidder ; who can not bid .
The printing of ballots is not within this section.
Krieger v. Standard Printing Co., 191 Ky . 552, 231
S. W. 27 .
§248. Grand jury; number ;trialjury in
inferiorcourts; majority verdict.
The questionwhether a woman may be a juror
willnot be decided on an appeal from a conviction
for crime. McLaughlin v. Com ., 192 Ky . 206, 232
S. W. 628 .
The provisionsof § 41 of the Act of March 22,
1922, (с.33, p.109), relatingto liquors, which au-
thorizeprosecutionsin courtswhere there are only
sixmembers of a jury,are constitutional. Lakes v.
Goodloe,195 Ky . 240, 242 S. W. 632.In condemnation proceedingsthe verdictof the
jury must be unanimous. City of Hazard v.Combs ,
213 Ky . 750 , 281 S W. 993 .
§ 249. Officersand employees of general
assembly ; number allowed.
Neither body of the general assembly may hire
jointlyor severallyany help other than that speci-
fiedin thissection. Shanks , auditorv. Julian, 213
Ky .291,280 S. W. 1081.
This section does not create the positions therein
mentioned nor require their filling. Shanks v .
Howes ,214 Ky .613,283 S.W. 966.
§ 252. House of reform to be established.
A child committed to the house of reform by a
countycourt,asdelinquent,isnota personwho hasbeen convictedof a felonyor a misdemeanor . The
county may be required to reimburse the Common-
wealth for the maintenance of such child. Lang
v . Com ., 190 Ky . 29, 226 S. W. 379 .
§254. Disciplineand suppliesfor con-
victs; statetocontrol.
The Act of March 17 , 1914 , (c.26, p .154 ), as to
inmates of house of reform, is valid. Lang , judge
v . Com ., 190 Ky . 29, 226 S. W. 379 .

The damages to be recoveredby a widow under
this section are such damages as she would sustain
by the destruction of her husband's power to earn
money . Souther v.Belleau,203 Ky . 508, 262 S. W.

Burden is not on plaintiff to negative self de-

not to be credited on a claim against a railroad com-
pany under Federal Employers ' Liability Act (U.
S. Comp .Stats. 8657-8665), for loss of the same life.
Chesapeake & Ohio Railway Co. v . Maggard's admr .;
Maggard's admr . v . Chesapeake & Ohio Railway

proximate cause was an unlawful employment . If

the employment and permitted same , the action
cannot be maintained . Cincinnati Times -Star Co.
v . Clay's admr ., 195 Ky . 465 , 243 S. W. 16 .
A wife , and if dead her administrator, is entitled
to the damages for the death of the husband , al-
though the wife in his lifetime deserted him and
lived in adultery, § 2133 not being applicable. Na-
pier'sAdmr . v. Napier's Admr ., 210 Ky . 163, 275

§ 11. Actions to quiet title; judgment .
Proof of actual possession by plaintiff is not
necessary, if defendant by way of counter-claim
asks to be adjudged the owner of the land. Cooper
v.Williamson,191 Ky .213,229 S. W. 707.
An action to cancel a deed need not allege pos-
session. Big Sandy Co. v.Abshire, 200 Ky .38, 252
S. W. 108 .
Though plaintifffailsto show possession, if de-
fendant by counter -claim asserts titleand seeks af-
firmativerelief, court will pass on superiorityof
title. Osborn v . Osborn , 204 Ky . 144, 263 S.W. 738 .
To sustain an action to quiet titleplaintiffmust
prove both title and actual possession of land .
Leach v. Taylor, 206 Ky . 28, 266 S.W. 894.
An action for injury to real property may be
maintained in any county in which any part of the
tractlies. Collinsv. Adams , 207 Ky . 42, 268 S.W.
828 .
In an action to quiet titleunder this section if
the defendants do not set up any counter -claim ask-
ing for affirmative relief, the plaintiffmust allege
and prove both titleand possession. Boreing v .Gar-
rard, 210 Ky . 135 , 275 S.W. 374 .
In a suit to quiet titlewhere the answer contains
a counter -claim also seeking to quiet titlethe court
will adjudge the titlealthough the plaintifffails to
show possession. Burger v . Allen , 211 Ky . 742 , 277
S.W. 1032 .
Suit under this section may be maintained with-
out reference to time when possession of titlewas
acquired . Lauderbach v . Lewis , 214 Ky . 521, 283
S. W. 973 .

§ 69. Controversies which may be sub-
mitted ; how submission made .
Common law right to submit controversies to arbi-

Gannon v. McClannahan , 204 Ky . 67, 263 S.W. 770.
§ 71. Arbitrators; duty ;noticeof time and
place of meeting ; selectionof umpire .
Where arbitrators cannot agree and an umpire is
chosen , it is his duty to make award as if he were
the sole arbitrator, and the originalarbitrators
should not participate after they disagree or join
with umpire in award . Sea v. Larimore, 205 Ky .
528, 266 S.W. 56.
§ 72. Award to be in writing; copies de-
liveredto parties; action on award .
(a) Failure of the written award to state that
arbitrators had disagreed and the award was made
by the umpire did not invalidateit. (b ) Where the
arbitrators joined with the umpire in signing an
award made by him alone, theirjoiningmay be re-
jectedas surplusage. Sea v.Larimore,205 Ky .528,
266 S.W. 56 .
Where the arbitratorsdisagree and the award was
by the umpire alone, though one arbitratorsigned
with him , party was not entitled to have umpire ,
and arbitrators reassembled to amend such award ,
because had both arbitrators signed it would have
only evidenced the fact of their disagreement andthat the award was solely that of the umpire . Sea
v .Larimore,205 Ky .528,266 S.W. 56.

ing;waiting-rooms and closets.
The violation of this section and the violation of
K. S. § 784 cannotproperlybe joinedin an indict
ment . Although a waiting room is too small for

section is not violated thereby , if it is not too small
for the accommodation of passengers . Common-
wealth v. L. & N. R. R. Co., 191 Ky . 634, 231 S.

If the closet be locked the keys to it must be
accessible. They may be left with the agent ; but
if he be absent , they must be where they may be
readily seen and obtained . Commonwealth v .Louis-
ville& I.Railway Co.,190 Ky . 39, 226 S. W. 105 .
The Railroad Commission has no authority to
order a rebuilding of a station unless same has been
burned or otherwise destroyed ; but if a station
has become unfit for the accommodation of the pub-
lic the commission may order a repairing of same .

ARTICLE XIX .
Co -Operative Marketing Associations
§ 883f-1. Declarationof policy. In order
to promote ,fosterand encourage the intelli-
gentand orderlymarketingof agricultural
products through co-operation; and to elim-
inate speculation and waste ; and to make
the distributionof agriculturalproducts be-
tween producer and consumer as direct as
can be efficientlydone ; and to stabilize the
marketing of agriculturalproducts,thisAct
ispassed. (January 10,1922,с.1,p .2, § 1.)
See also Ky . Stat. § 4636g -1 relating to co-opera-
tive marketing bureau .
The validity of this statute including the pro-
vision of subsection 18 for an injunction was sus-
tained. This decision was rendered in a proceeding
under the declaratoryjudgmentof 1922, c. 83,
p . 235. Potter v . Dark Tobacco Growers Co -opera-
tive association, 201 Ky . 441 , 257 S. W. 33.
This act is not special legislation within the
meaning of section 59 of our Constitution. Liberty
Warehouse Co. v. Burley Tobacco Growers ' Co-
operative Association , 208 Ky . 643, 271 S.W. 695 .
§ 883f-2 . Definitions.- As used in thisact.
(a) The term "agriculturalproducts"shallinclude horticultural, viticultural, for-
estry,dairy,livestock,poultry,bee and any
farm products .
(b ) The term " member " shallinclude ac-
tualmembersofassociationswithoutcapitalstock and holders of common stock in associ-
ationsorganized with capitalstock.
(c) The term " association" means any
corporationorganized under thisact; and
(d ) The term " person " shall include in-
dividuals, firms, partnerships, corporations
and associations .
Associationsorganized hereunder shallbe
deemed " non -profit," inasmuch as they are
not organized to make profitfor themselves,
as such, or for their members , as such, but
only for theirmembers as producers.
(e) For the purpose of brevity and con-
venience thisAct may be indexed, referred
toandcitedas"TheBinghamCo-operativeMarketingAct." (January10,1922,c.1,p.3,§ 2.)
§ 883f-3. Who may organize.- Twenty
(20) or more persons,a majority of whom are
residentsofthisstate,engagedintheproduc-
tionof agriculturalproducts, may form a
non -profit, co-operative association, with or
without capitalstock,under the provisionsof
thisAct . (January 10,1922,с.1,p.3,§ 3.)
§ 883f-4. Purposes .- An associationmay
be organizedto engage in any activityin
connection with the marketing or sellingof
the agriculturalproductsof itsmembers ,or
with the harvesting, preserving, drying,
processing, canning, packing, grading, stor-
ing,handling,shipping or utilizationthereof,
or the manufacturing or marketing of the
by-productsthereof; or in connectionwith
themanufacturing,sellingor supplyingto
itsmembers of machinery ,equipment or sup-
plies; or in the financingof the above enu-
merated activities; or in any one or more of
the activitiesspecifiedherein. (January 10,
1922 ,с.1,p .3, § 4.)
§883f-5. Preliminary investigation.—
Every group of persons contemplating the
organizationof an associationunder thisact
isurged to communicate with the Dean of the
College of Agriculture of the University of
Kentucky ,who willinformthem whatever a
survey of the marketing conditionsaffecting
the commodities proposed to be handled may
indicateregarding probable success.
It is here recognized that agriculture is
characterizedby individualproduction in
contrastto the group or factory system that
characterizesother forms of industrialpro-
duction; and thattheordinaryformof
corporate organization permits industrial
groups to combine for the purpose of group
productionand the ensuinggroup marketing
and that the public has an interestin permit-
tingfarmerstobringtheirindustrytothe
high degree of efficiencyand merchandising
skill evidenced in the manufacturing indus-
tries; and that the public interesturgently
needs to prevent the migration from the farm
to the cityin order to keep up farm produc-
tion and to preserve the agriculturalsupply
of the nation; and that the public interest
demands that the farmer be encouraged to
attain a superior and more directsystem of
marketing in the substitutionof merchandis-
ing for the blind,unscientificand speculative
sellingof crops; and that for this purpose ,
the farmers should secure special guidance
and instructive data from the Dean of the
CollegeofAgricultureoftheUniversityofKentucky.(January10,1922,с.1,p.4,§5.)

§ 884. Poor person allowed to sue without
paying .
A person convicted of a felony prayed the cir-
cuit court to be allowed to prosecute in forma pau-
peris. This was refused. He had a right to a rule
from a court of appeals against the clerk and the
reporter to be allowed to prosecute without prepay-
ment of fees. Smith v.Bastin, 192 Ky .164, 232 S.
W. 415 .
§ 885. Commonwealth not liablefor costs.
Land owner appealing from judgment affirming
findings as to violation of land obtained a con-
siderable reduction, but he is not entitled to recover
his costs from the board of supervisors for the state
and he should not be charged with costs incurred
by them . Brown v . Wayne County Board of Super-
visors; 204 Ky . 550 ; 264 S.W. 1073 .
§ 886. Criminal prosecutions; defendant
when liable for costs .
Defendant convicted of felony is liable for all
costs of prosecution . Frazier v . Toliver, 204 Ky . 79 ;
263 S.W. 713 .
§ 889. Ordinary and equity action; nom-
inalparties; partners, jointtenants; settle-
ments .
A judgment of a circuit court properly awarded
a mandamus against the state board of charities
and corrections as to payments to convicts. Pend-
ing an appeal the Statute of 1916 , (K. S. § 3828a , of
Supplement of 1918), was repealed. The judgment
was reversed; but the appellantrequiredto pay the
cost in both courts . State Board of Charities v .
Combs , 190 Ky . 147 , 227 S. W. 282 .
§ 891. Appeal to court of appeals;discre-
tion on reversal .
A judgment of a circuitcourt properly awarded
a mandamus against the state board of charities
and corrections. Pending an appeal the Act of 1916,
(K. S. § 3828a7, of Supplement of 1918), was re-
pealed. The judgment was reversed. Appellant
was required to pay the costs in both courts. State
Board of Charities v Hays ; State Board of Chari-
ties v . Combs , 190 Ky . 147 , 227 S. W. 282.
§ 900. Divorce and alimony .
Where the wife in a divorce suit is not in fault,
the husband must pay all costs, including attorney's
fees. Ratliffv .Ratliff,193 Ky .738 , 237 S. W. 397.
A certain wife did not have ample estate to pay
the costs of a divorce action. Hoffman v . Hoffman ,
190 Ky . 13, 226 S. W. 119. A certainwife had
ample means to pay the costs. Kunze v . Kunze ,
191 Ky . 256, 229 S. W. 1031 .
The court of appeals ordered a husband under
specialcircumstancesto pay a reasonableattorney's
fees for presenting the appeal of his wife from a
judgment in a case in which he procured a divorce,
and her counter claim was not sustained by the
circuitcourt. Krieger v . Krieger , 194 Ky . 812 , 241
S. W. 828 .
A certain wife was not at fault. Gibson v Gibson ,
199 Ky .257, 250 S. W. 986 .
If a wife is not in fault, the husband is liable
for her costs in the divorce action including an
attorney's fee. If there be no testimony as to
value of services of attorney , the chancellor may
fix it from an inspection of the record. Heskamp
v .Heskamp , 203 Ky . 75, 261 S. W. 848 .
Court erred in directing execution for cost and
attorney's fees against a defendant constructively
summoned . Vogt v . Vogt , 205 Ky . 569, 266 S.W. 49 .
Where the husband is entitled to divorce and the
wife has ample estate of her own , the husband need
not pay her attorney'sfees. Ward v. Ward , 213
Ky . 606 , 281 S. W. 801 .
§ 904. Attorney's fee; taxation of costs;
copies of pleadings; witnesses.
Although the court may not limit the number of
witnesses he may refuse to tax as costs more than
allowance to two . Axton v . Vance , 207 Ky . 580,
269 S.W. 534 .

§ 1456. Certificatesand petitionsto be
filed before election .
Filing of the certificateof nomination with the
county clerk as required by the statutes is manda-
tory and unless complied with the clerk has no

certificateis sufficient. Where the nominee pre-
sented his certificate of nomination to the clerk and

§ 1639. Death presumed after absence of
seven years .
The seven years absence was shown . The burden
thereupon was on the person attacking the presump-
tion of death. Duncan v. Clore, 189 Ky . 132, 224
S. W. 678 .
In the absence of evidence tending to show an
earlierdeath of the absentee, it will be presumed
that he liveduntilthe end of the seven years, but
proof of circumstances such as age or physical con-
dition may authorize a finding of an earlierdate of
death . Glasscock v . Weare , 192 Ky . 654, 234 S. W.
216 .
The presumption of death does not arise until
the full statutory period has elapsed, unless this
presumption is overcome by evidence tending to
show a prior death . Mutual Life Insurance Co. of
N. Y. v.LouisvilleTrust Co., 207 Ky .654,269 S.W.
1014.This statute does not apply to non residents. Pool
v .Pool , 214 Ky .267 ,283 S.W. 111 .

v.Commonwealth ,211 Ky .594,277 S. W. 980.

Husband and wife had two sons . The wife deed
seised of land in fee . The husband took a home-
stead under K. S. § 1708. This did not merge in the
fee when the two sons died successively. He took
also under K. S. § 1702 a homestead in the undivided
one -half which descended to him in fee on the death
of the first son . As after the death of his second
son, he had no family, he did not take a homestead
under K. S. §1702 on the other undivided half.

S. W. 363 .
In settingup the homestead exemption,the excep-
tion should be negatived . This is a change of the
rule under the general statutes. Marshall v . Tully,
193 Ky . 246, 235 S. W. 726 .
A general creditor may not require a lienholder to
collect his debt out of the homestead exemption .
Baker v .Davis ,203 Ky .221, 262 S. W. 3 .
Homestead not abandoned by enforced confine-
ment in penitentiary. Clolingerv. Callahan, 204

One may sell homestead and re-invest proceeds
without affecting its immunity from seizure under
execution. Clolingerv. Callahan, 204 Ky . 33, 263

Allotment of homestead by appraisers is subject

& Co. v .Noe , 208 Ky . 314 , 270 S. W. 799 .
Where the debtor is entitled to his homestead

Temporary absences from the property with in-
tention to return will not operate as an abandon-

226 , 277 S. W. 245 .

Homestead should be allowed in life estate sold

§1708. Right ofhusband tohomesteadof
wife .
A woman seised of land in fee died intestate

A husband and wife jointly owned a fifty acre

Charboneau v. Hart, 211 Ky . 204, 277 S. W. 242.
§ 1709. Rights of purchaser ; creditor;
defendant may redeem ; purchaser of person-
alty to give bond ; controlof courts over.
An execution sale of encumbered land created a

Kennedy Co. v . Cooper , 189 Ky . 366 ,224 S. W. 1053 .

set aside; practice; when liennot affected.
A venditioni may be obtained by motion in a

§ 2554a -24. Drinking or drunk in public
place; misdemeanor .- Any person who shall
in any public place, or in or upon any pas-
senger coach, streetcar, or in or upon any
vehicle commonly used for the transporta-
tion of passengers, or in or about any depot,
platform,waitingstationor room,drinkany
intoxicatingliquorof any kind, or if any
person shallbe drunk or intoxicatedin any
public or private road, or in any passenger
coach, streetcar, or other public place or
building, or at any public gathering, or if
any person shall be drunk or intoxicated,
and shalldisturbthepeaceof any person,he
shallbe guilty of a misdemeanor and upon
convictionthereof shallbe punished by fine
of not less than ten dollars nor more than
onehundred dollars,or by imprisonmentfor
not lessthan fivedays nor more than thirty
days, or by both such fineand imprison-
ment . (March 22,1922,c. 33,p .109, § 24.)
The offenseof being drunk on a road has a natural
connection with the subject expressed in the title
of the act . This subsection is valid . Com . v . Rob-
inson,192 Ky . 374,233 S. W. 790.
Mere drunkenness does not violate this statute .
Maynard v.Com .,202 Ky .684,261 S. W. 10.
It is not an offense for a private citizen to be
drunk unless at one of the places or gatherings in-
cluded in this section. No peace bond can be re-
quired of him because of such drunkenness . Com .
v . Adams , 201 Ky . 421, 257 S. W. 45; Morgan v.
Com ., and Maggard v.Com .,202 Ky .211,259 S. W.46 .
Prosecution for drunkenness under this subsec-
tion, must be brought within six months . If the
averment fixes a day that in fact is within six
months , the indictment is not invalidatedby the
statement that it was within twelve months . Mul-
lins v . Com ., 203 Ky . 790, 263 S. W. 350 .
Prosecution for being drunk on public road must
be begun within six months. Smith v. Com ., 204
Ky . 448 , 264 S. W. 1047 .
The offenseof drunkennessisno longera public
offenseunlesscommitted in a publicplace. Hark-
leroadv.Com .,207 Ky .552, 269 S. W. 724.

reasonably necessary to carry out and per-

ders for the performance of duty in connec-

jority of the members shall constitute a

CHAPTER 106 .
RECORDS - HOW LOST SUPPLIED
§ 3993. County court; lost or mutilated
orderor bond in; supplied.
Where bond of guardian was lost, infant could
sue thereon without supplying lostbond in the man-
ner provided by this section, there being a copy of
the bond in the bond book to which the county
judge could testify. Upchurch v. Helton, 205 Ky .
192, 265 S. W. 770 .
§3998. Originalrecords or copiesmay be
recordedagain ; effect.
A county clerk's officeburned ; the grantee in one
of the deeds forbore for an unreasonable time to
record it. Meanwhile the apparent owners con-
veyed for value such interest in the land as they
had inherited. The vendee was not a bona fidepur-
chaser of the land . The original grantee was not
barred by his laches. Swango v .Kentucky Coal and
Lumber Development Co., 200 Ky . 522 , 255 S.-W.
114 .
§ 4010. Authentication of records .
A party is not guilty of want of diligence in
failing to examine the original records to see wheth-
er a certifiedcopy is correct, as he is entitled to rely
on such certifiedcopy as being correct. Brandon
v .Butler , 212 Ky . 76 , 278 S. W. 156 .

§4526b-1. High schools;concerning;duty
of the county board of education.
The county board of education is required to
maintain a high school at the county seat or arrange
for high school facilities, failing which it is liable
for tuition of pupils entitled to attend such high
school. Christian County Board of Education v .
Morris , 207 Ky . 221 , 268 S. W. 1106 .
Although the county board of education does not
maintain a high schoolat the county seat,it isnot
required to pay tuition for children in the city high
school at such county seat where an adequate and
accessible high school is established in the school
district in which they live. Scott County Board of
Education v.Crumbaugh ,213 Ky .771,281 S.W. 977.

Written notice of injury is unnecessary where

injury, and claim for compensation is made within

Emmons , 205 Ky . 21, 265 S. W. 447 .
Where the obligation to pay compensation ter-
minated on death of employee , the payment by

Mining Co. v.Fowler,208 Ky .422, 271 S. W. 589.
Limitations are not tolled because children are
minors , where widow is sui juris. Ashland Iron &
Mining Co. v.Fowler,208 Ky .422,271 S. W. 589.
An employee who gave notice of his injury within

injury. Kingston-Pocahontas Coal Co. v. Maynard ,

The words " voluntarilypaid" in this section

Claim for compensationheld made too late. Kirk ,

Sufficiencyof applicationfor compensation isnot
